summary: This diff (the full dispatch/status consolidation branch, including the round-2 bug fix) is sound. The core fix is correct: dispatch_core._upsert_wiring_row() previously called only _ensure_wiring_registry_table() (a no-op CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS against an existing table), never the real _migrate_wiring_registry_entity_types() CHECK-widening migration, so every record_dispatch_event() write against production's pre-migration schema raised a silently-swallowed IntegrityError. The fix adds the missing migration call directly (bypassing the broader _migrate_schema() to avoid touching the unrelated system_index table, which is a reasonable, narrowly-scoped choice), and is backed by a genuine regression test that seeds a fixture DB with the real narrower pre-migration CHECK constraint, confirms the write is queryable afterward, and confirms a pre-existing row survives the table-rebuild migration unchanged. I verified the migration function itself (rebuild table with widened CHECK, copy rows, rebuild FTS5 index+triggers, idempotent no-op once migrated) is implemented correctly in scripts/superboss-register.py. The companion round-2 fix (module_queue_tick round-robin across module queues instead of draining one module's queue before the next) is also correct and has its own targeted regression test. I ran the full test suite (85 tests including the new multi-process concurrency-lock proof) and all pass. No shell=True/os.system/eval, no SQL built from user-controlled input (entity_type list is a static constant), no .github/workflows/** changes, and no touches to migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security paths, consistent with the pre-classified tier1 rating. The 6 superseded scripts are renamed (not deleted) per the stated task scope, preserving history, and are confirmed unwired from anything else in the repo.
